exposure: Febrile illness or antibiotic use in the 2 weeks prior to presentation
cohort: 365 women with confirmed severe maternal sepsis and 757 controls from all UK obstetrician-led maternity units
finding: The incidence of severe sepsis was 4.7 per 10,000 maternities, with genital tract infection and Escherichia coli being the most common source and organism, respectively, and several risk factors were identified.
mod_finding: Women who had an operative vaginal delivery, pre-labour cesarean section, or cesarean section after labour onset had significantly increased odds of severe sepsis.
